opposition.case_against: The thesis rests on a stale number. The 94% December-hike probability comes from the 14 October Citi/FedWatch note that followed the hot September CPI. Trading Economics puts December odds at about 84% on 10 November, up from about 74% a week earlier, and they fell as low as about 68-77% around the midterms. Hawkish repricing still has room to run, and the move is already in that direction. The labour data argue against a benign path: October payrolls were +165K against a 65K forecast, unemployment fell to 4.1%, jobless claims are at a 57-year low, productivity beat, and markets already price a further hike in 2027. The 10y depends on that terminal path, not only on the December decision. Inflation momentum is also adverse. September headline CPI was 3.7% (expected 3.6%) and core rose from 2.4% to 2.6% with a 0.3% m/m print, so price pressure is spreading beyond energy. The consensus for October already expects easing, which means a benign print is largely priced, while a core miss gets the trade stopped out. The oil leg is the weakest part.
